title: Deciphering Cellular Pathology: Soft X-ray Tomography as a Tool for Disease Research
content: Understanding cellular pathology is a cornerstone of disease research, as subtle changes in morphology or in the three-dimensional (3D) distribution of components within cells often underpin the onset and progression of various illnesses. Soft X-ray Tomography (SXT) stands out as an advanced imaging technique that enables 3D visualization of cellular structures without the need for labels or extensive sample preparation [1, 2]. By using soft X-rays in the "water-window" range, SXT produces high-contrast images that clearly reveal detailed subcellular ultrastructures. In addition, SXT provides quantitative information through the linear absorption coefficient (LAC), a parameter directly correlated with biomolecular density. This capability allows researchers to measure and analyze cellular alterations with precision, making SXT a valuable tool for investigating disease-related changes in cell architecture. This quantitative approach is crucial for cell biologists as they decipher the mechanisms underlying various diseases, including cancer metastasis, the formation of biomolecular condensates associated with Parkinson’s disease, and virus-host interactions. Overall, the integration of SXT into cellular pathology research offers a powerful means to uncover and quantify the subtle structural changes that drive disease, ultimately paving the way for improved diagnostics and targeted therapies.
